nodes.title: Strict Banach Galois representations
nodes.statement: For a profinite G_K, B(G_K) has Q_p-Banach spaces up to equivalent norms with jointly continuous linear action, and continuous equivariant linear maps. A conflation is an algebraically exact sequence 0→W_1→W→W_2→0 of these maps; equivalently the first map identifies the closed kernel topologically and the second is an open surjection. This is an exact category. The imported almost C category is its full subcategory, with the same strict sequences.
hypotheses: K satisfies the general base convention; no finiteness over Q_p is needed for this ambient exact category.
proofSteps: Use continuous linear maps on Banach carriers, with continuous action as extra structure; import the finite-dimensional representation category from R01.1.

Apply the native Banach open mapping theorem to the surjection and the bijection onto its closed kernel. Kernels are closed and complete. Pullbacks of open surjections and pushouts of closed embeddings give the exact-category axioms.
acceptance: A short exact sequence of finite-dimensional representations has its usual exact structure.

nodes.title: Almost-split extensions
nodes.statement: For finite K/Q_p, an extension in B(G_K) of two almost C-representations has almost C middle term if and only if it is almost split: there is a finite-dimensional stable Q_p-subspace Z of the kernel such that the pushed-out sequence after quotienting by Z admits a continuous equivariant splitting. nodes.title: Topological Vector Spaces
nodes.statement: A Topological Vector Space is a covariant functor W:Symp_C→LH(C_Qp), with Q_p-linear structure maps, such that for every Λ,Λ′ and bounded subset A of W(Λ), the union of u_*(A) over all continuous C-algebra maps u:Λ→Λ′ is bounded in W(Λ′). Morphisms are natural transformations. Exactness means exactness in the left heart at every Λ. Hom and Ext^i_TVS mean natural maps and Yoneda extensions for this exact structure. Boundedness is interpreted in the classical quotient realization of a left-heart object, retaining its non-Hausdorff quotient topology; verify independence of the injective presentation.

nodes.title: The explicit perfectoid cover of the unit disc
nodes.statement: For odd p choose compatible p-power roots of p and set Y_n=(E_(1/p^n)−1)/p^(1/p^(n+1)). The ring O_C{X}[Y_n:n≥0] is integral over O_C{X}; its p-adic completion is perfectoid. proofSteps: Subtract the constant cocycle. Integrate the first Y-derivative to find u formally; the cocycle identity forces the remaining homogeneous pieces to vanish.

For a nonnormalized constant c, add −c to the primitive, since the coboundary of a constant is its negative.

nodes.title: Reasonable C-spaces
nodes.statement: A reasonable C-space is a Hausdorff locally convex C-vector space, separable in the sense of a dense C-linear subspace of countable dimension, together with a Fréchet presentation or a countable compact-type presentation. Its TVS realization is Λ↦Λ completed-projective-tensor_C W. The two types are remembered when a same-type theorem is used.
hypotheses: C need not be spherically complete; L0 theorems requiring spherical completeness cannot simply be specialized to C.

Use countable-type Banach models and completed projective tensors to construct the realization. Verify independence from the Banach/seminorm presentation and C-evaluation.
Keep the compact-type extension closure gap G-COMPACT and the Fréchet passage G-FRECHET explicit.

nodes.title: Normalized period pushout extensions
nodes.statement: For a topological B_m-model W, d≥1 and w∈W, push out 0→B_m --t^d→B_(m+d)→B_d→0 along c↦cw. The sign is the usual pushout convention, so E_1 for W=C,d=m=1 is B_2 with its specified endpoints. The class depends on w modulo t^dW and induces Ext^1_B(B_d,W)≅W/t^dW; for the topological exact structure prove the indicated classes are strict and all extensions admit the compatible topology. This proof is separate from TVS essential surjectivity.

Check continuity for the finitely generated source and quotient topologies before comparison with TVS.

nodes.title: A profinite cocycle lies in one compact-type step
nodes.statement: If H is profinite, W=ind_n W_n is a compact-type inductive limit of C-Banach spaces, and H acts compatibly and isometrically on every W_n, every continuous 1-cocycle H→W has image in a single W_N. The assertion concerns cocycles with these invariant steps, not every continuous map to an arbitrary inductive limit.
hypotheses: The compact/c-compact closure properties of unit balls must hold for the chosen presentation.
proofSteps: Let B_n be the closed image of the unit ball and form the increasing closed subgroups U_n=Σ_(i≤n) p^(i−n) B_i covering W.
The inverse images H_n of U_n under the cocycle are closed subgroups, by the isometric action and cocycle equation. Baire gives one H_n with nonempty interior, hence finite index.
Adjoin finitely many coset representatives’ cocycle values and use the cocycle equation to find one common W_N.
acceptance: A constant zero cocycle lies in every step; nonisometric, noninvariant steps do not meet the hypotheses.

nodes.title: Filtered quasi–Banach–Colmez spaces
nodes.statement: A qBC object is a TVS W equipped with subobjects 0⊂W_{>0}⊂W_{≥0}⊂W such that W_{>0} is a classical BC of curvature >0, W_{=0}=W_{≥0}/W_{>0} is a period Pair, and W_{<0}=W/W_{≥0} is a classical BC of curvature <0. A morphism is a TVS map preserving both subobjects and inducing a period-linear Pair map on the middle quotient. Its integer height is ht(W_{>0})+ht(W_{<0}). Curvature >0, ≥0, =0, <0, ≤0 means respectively W=W_{>0}, W=W_{≥0}, the two outer graded pieces vanish, W_{≥0}=0, and W_{>0}=0. A qBC is reasonable when its middle Pair is reasonable; two reasonable qBC objects have the same type when their middle presentations have a common branch as in VectorBundlesAndIsocrystalsPartII:TVS.2/reasonable-pairs.
hypotheses: All subobjects and quotients are in the pointwise left-heart exact structure.
Intrinsic uniqueness of the filtration is asserted only with reasonableness, by VectorBundlesAndIsocrystalsPartII:QBC.0/intrinsic-curvature-filtration.
proofSteps: Use the imported classical BC embedding into TVS and VectorBundlesAndIsocrystalsPartII:TVS.0/period-pairs for the middle piece. Define composition and identities by the filtered maps and Pair morphisms.
Height is invariant under filtered isomorphism because the two outer BC pieces are then isomorphic; use the parent invariant, without inventing a finite dimension for the middle Pair.

Embed a classical BC using its parent canonical curvature filtration. Its middle affine BC is a finite-length period Module and therefore a Pair [0→M]. The old and new heights agree because affine BCs have height zero.
acceptance: Height is invariant under qBC isomorphism; invariance under underlying TVS isomorphisms requires VectorBundlesAndIsocrystalsPartII:QBC.0/qbc-forgetful-full-faithfulness.
The middle graded piece need not have finite length or a numerical C-dimension.
